study type: Cost-minimisation analysis, comparative cohort study with propensity score matching
outcome: Cost per birth (total, hospital, patient travel)
cohort: The participants were women with a singleton pregnancy who received antenatal care and birthed at Monash Health, divided into pre-telehealth (Jan 2018-Mar 2020) and post-telehealth (Apr 2020-Dec 2021) cohorts.
finding: Telehealth-integrated antenatal care supported the provision of a greater volume of antenatal care to more complex pregnancies, while maintaining safety and quality of care, for only a minimal cost increase to health funders and substantial cost savings to patients.
mod_finding: The post-telehealth cohort showed increased rates of caesarean birth.
